sanskrit: susūkṣmo 'pīha dehe vai śalyo janayate rujam kiṃ punaḥ śarasaṃghātaiś citasya tava bhārata
english: Even a very fine splinter lodged in the body breeds pain; how much more for you, O Bhārata, pierced through and through by a mass of arrows.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ naitat tavākhyeyaṃ prāṇināṃ prabhavāpyayau bhavān hy upadiśec chreyo devānām api bhārata
english: Truly there is no need to instruct you on the origin and dissolution of living beings, for you, O Bhārata, could teach the highest good even to the gods.

sanskrit: yad dhi bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca bhavac ca puruṣarṣabha sarvaṃ taj jñānavṛddhasya tava pāṇāv ivāhitam
english: For whatever has been, will be, and now is, O bull among men, all of it lies as if placed in your palm, ripe with wisdom as you are.

sanskrit: saṃsāraś caiva bhūtānāṃ dharmasya ca phalodayaḥ viditas te mahāprājña tvaṃ hi brahmamayo nidhiḥ
english: The cycle of transmigration of beings and the ripening of the fruit of dharma are known to you, O man of great wisdom; you are a treasury made of brahman.

sanskrit: tvāṃ hi rājye sthitaṃ sphīte samagrāṅgam arogiṇam strīsahasraiḥ parivṛtaṃ paśyāmīhordhvaretasam
english: For though set in a flourishing kingdom, whole of limb and free of sickness, surrounded by a thousand women, I see you here as one whose seed flows ever upward, chaste.

sanskrit: ṛte śāṃtanavād bhīṣmāt triṣu lokeṣu pārthiva satyasaṃdhān mahāvīryāc chūrād dharmaikatatparāt
english: In the three worlds, O king, save for Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu—true to his word, of mighty valor, heroic, devoted to dharma alone—

sanskrit: mṛtyum āvārya tarasā śaraprastaraśāyinaḥ nisargaprabhavaṃ kiṃ cin na ca tātānuśuśruma
english: of no one have we ever heard, dear sire, who, lying on a bed of arrows, has by sheer power held off death that arises by nature's own course.

sanskrit: satye tapasi dāne ca yajñādhikaraṇe tathā dhanurvede ca vede ca nityaṃ caivānvavekṣaṇe
english: In truth, in austerity, in giving, in the conduct of sacrifice, in the science of archery and in the Veda, and ever in vigilant discernment—

sanskrit: anṛśaṃsaṃ śuciṃ dāntaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratam mahārathaṃ tvatsadṛśaṃ na kaṃ cid anuśuśruma
english: of no great chariot-warrior like you have we ever heard: free of cruelty, pure, self-controlled, devoted to the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi devān sagandharvān sasurāsurarākṣasān śakta ekarathenaiva vijetuṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: For you are able, with but a single chariot, to conquer the gods together with the gandharvas, the suras, asuras, and rākṣasas—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi bhīṣma mahābāho vasūnāṃ vāsavopamaḥ nityaṃ vipraiḥ samākhyāto navamo 'navamo guṇaiḥ
english: For you, O mighty-armed Bhīṣma, are the peer of Vāsava among the Vasus; ever do the brāhmaṇas declare you the ninth, yet second to none in your virtues.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi tvābhijānāmi yas tvaṃ puruṣasattama tridaśeṣv api vikhyātaḥ svaśaktyā sumahābalaḥ
english: For I know you well, O best of men—you who by your own power are renowned even among the thirty gods, you of surpassing might.

sanskrit: manuṣyeṣu manuṣyendra na dṛṣṭo na ca me śrutaḥ bhavato yo guṇais tulyaḥ pṛthivyāṃ puruṣaḥ kva cit
english: Among men, O lord of men, never have I seen nor heard of any man anywhere on earth who is your equal in virtues.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi sarvair guṇai rājan devān apy atiricyase tapasā hi bhavāñ śaktaḥ sraṣṭuṃ lokāṃś carācarān
english: For in all virtues, O king, you surpass even the gods; indeed, by your austerity you are able to create the worlds with all that moves and is still.

sanskrit: tad asya tapyamānasya jñātīnāṃ saṃkṣayeṇa vai jyeṣṭhasya pāṇḍuputrasya śokaṃ bhīṣma vyapānuda
english: Therefore, O Bhīṣma, drive away the grief of this eldest son of Pāṇḍu, who burns with sorrow over the destruction of his kinsmen.

sanskrit: ye hi dharmāḥ samākhyātāś cāturvarṇyasya bhārata cāturāśramyasaṃsṛṣṭās te sarve viditās tava
english: For all the dharmas declared for the four varṇas, O Bhārata, intertwined with those of the four stages of life, are known to you.

sanskrit: cāturvedye ca ye proktāś cāturhotre ca bhārata sāṃkhye yoge ca niyatā ye ca dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: Those duties proclaimed in the fourfold Vedic lore and in the fourfold priestly office, O Bhārata, and those eternal dharmas fixed in Sāṃkhya and Yoga—

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyena yaś caiko dharmo na sma virudhyate sevyamānaḥ sa caivādyo gāṅgeya viditas tava
english: and that one foremost dharma which, when practiced, stands unopposed by any of the four varṇas—that too, O son of Gaṅgā, is known to you.

sanskrit: itihāsapurāṇaṃ ca kārtsnyena viditaṃ tava dharmaśāstraṃ ca sakalaṃ nityaṃ manasi te sthitam
english: The lore of legend and ancient tale is known to you in its entirety, and the whole science of dharma stands ever fixed within your mind.

sanskrit: ye ca ke cana loke 'sminn arthāḥ saṃśayakārakāḥ teṣāṃ chettā nāsti loke tvad anyaḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: And whatever matters in this world breed doubt, there is no one in the world but you to cut them away, O bull among men.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍaveyasya manaḥsamutthitaṃ; narendra śokaṃ vyapakarṣa medhayā bhavadvidhā hy uttamabuddhivistarā; vimuhyamānasya janasya śāntaye
english: Therefore, O lord of men, draw out by your wisdom the grief that has risen in the mind of this son of Pāṇḍu; for one such as you, with the vast reach of supreme understanding, exists for the peace of bewildered folk.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā tu vacanaṃ bhīṣmo vāsudevasya dhīmataḥ kiṃ cid unnāmya vadanaṃ prāñjalir vākyam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of the wise Vāsudeva, Bhīṣma raised his face a little and, with palms joined, spoke these words.

sanskrit: namas te bhagavan viṣṇo lokānāṃ nidhanodbhava tvaṃ hi kartā hṛṣīkeśa saṃhartā cāparājitaḥ
english: Homage to you, O blessed Viṣṇu, source of the worlds' arising and ending; for you are their maker, O Hṛṣīkeśa, and their unconquered destroyer.

sanskrit: viśvakarman namas te 'stu viśvātman viśvasaṃbhava apavargo 'si bhūtānāṃ pañcānāṃ parataḥ sthitaḥ
english: O maker of all, homage be to you, O Self of all, source of all; you are the final release of beings, abiding beyond the five elements.

sanskrit: namas te triṣu lokeṣu namas te paratas triṣu yogeśvara namas te 'stu tvaṃ hi sarvaparāyaṇam
english: Homage to you in the three worlds, homage to you beyond the three; O Lord of Yoga, homage be to you, for you are the supreme refuge of all.

sanskrit: matsaṃśritaṃ yad āttha tvaṃ vacaḥ puruṣasattama tena paśyāmi te divyān bhāvān hi triṣu vartmasu
english: By the words you have spoken concerning me, O best of men, I now behold your divine manifestations along the three paths.

sanskrit: tac ca paśyāmi tattvena yat te rūpaṃ sanātanam sapta mārgā niruddhās te vāyor amitatejasaḥ
english: And I see in truth that eternal form of yours: the seven courses of the wind of boundless splendor are held fast within you.

sanskrit: divaṃ te śirasā vyāptaṃ padbhyāṃ devī vasuṃdharā diśo bhujau raviś cakṣur vīrye śakraḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: By your head the heaven is filled, by your feet the goddess Earth; the quarters are your arms, the sun your eye, and in your might stands Śakra established.

sanskrit: atasīpuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ pītavāsasam acyutam vapur hy anumimīmas te meghasyeva savidyutaḥ
english: We perceive your body, O Acyuta, dark as the flax-flower and robed in yellow, like a cloud charged with lightning.

sanskrit: tvatprapannāya bhaktāya gatim iṣṭāṃ jigīṣave yac chreyaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣa tad dhyāyasva surottama
english: For the devotee who has taken refuge in you and longs to win the desired goal, ponder, O lotus-eyed one, that which is his highest good, O best of the gods.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca yataḥ khalu parā bhaktir mayi te puruṣarṣabha tato vapur mayā divyaṃ tava rājan pradarśitam
english: Vāsudeva said: Because your devotion to me is supreme, O bull among men, therefore, O king, my divine form has been shown to you.

sanskrit: na hy abhaktāya rājendra bhaktāyānṛjave na ca darśayāmy aham ātmānaṃ na cādāntāya bhārata
english: For never, O lord of kings, do I reveal myself to one who is without devotion, nor to a devotee who is crooked, nor to one without self-restraint, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bhavāṃs tu mama bhaktaś ca nityaṃ cārjavam āsthitaḥ dame tapasi satye ca dāne ca nirataḥ śuciḥ
english: But you are my devotee, ever steadfast in uprightness, given to self-control, austerity, truth, and giving, and pure.

sanskrit: arhas tvaṃ bhīṣma māṃ draṣṭuṃ tapasā svena pārthiva tava hy upasthitā lokā yebhyo nāvartate punaḥ
english: You are worthy, O Bhīṣma, to behold me by your own austerity, O king; for there have drawn near to you those worlds from which one does not return again.

sanskrit: pañcāśataṃ ṣaṭ ca kurupravīra; śeṣaṃ dinānāṃ tava jīvitasya tataḥ śubhaiḥ karmaphalodayais tvaṃ; sameṣyase bhīṣma vimucya deham
english: Fifty-six days, O foremost hero of the Kurus, remain of your life; thereafter, O Bhīṣma, when you have let go the body, you shall attain to the auspicious risings of the fruits of your deeds.

sanskrit: ete hi devā vasavo vimānāny; āsthāya sarve jvalitāgnikalpāḥ antarhitās tvāṃ pratipālayanti; kāṣṭhāṃ prapadyantam udak pataṃgam
english: For these gods, the Vasus, all mounted in their celestial cars and blazing like fire, wait unseen upon you, until the sun, attaining its course, moves northward.

sanskrit: vyāvṛttamātre bhagavaty udīcīṃ; sūrye diśaṃ kālavaśāt prapanne gantāsi lokān puruṣapravīra; nāvartate yān upalabhya vidvān
english: The moment the blessed sun, by force of time, has turned and reached the northern quarter, you shall go, O foremost of heroes, to those worlds which the wise man, once he has gained, returns from no more.

sanskrit: amuṃ ca lokaṃ tvayi bhīṣma yāte; jñānāni naṅkṣyanty akhilena vīra ataḥ sma sarve tvayi saṃnikarṣaṃ; samāgatā dharmavivecanāya
english: And once you, O Bhīṣma, have departed this world, all knowledge will pass away entire, O hero; therefore have we all gathered close about you, for the discernment of dharma.

sanskrit: tajjñātiśokopahataśrutāya; satyābhisaṃdhāya yudhiṣṭhirāya prabrūhi dharmārthasamādhiyuktam; arthyaṃ vaco 'syāpanudāsya śokam
english: To Yudhiṣṭhira, true to his word, whose learning is stricken by grief for his kinsmen, speak the meaningful word joined to dharma, wealth, and concentration, and so dispel his sorrow.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kṛṣṇasya tad vākyaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ hitam śrutvā śāṃtanavo bhīṣmaḥ pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having heard those salutary words of Kṛṣṇa, joined with dharma and wealth, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu replied with palms joined.

sanskrit: lokanātha mahābāho śiva nārāyaṇācyuta tava vākyam abhiśrutya harṣeṇāsmi pariplutaḥ
english: O Lord of the worlds, mighty-armed, auspicious one, Nārāyaṇa, Acyuta—having heard your words, I am overwhelmed with joy.

sanskrit: kiṃ cāham abhidhāsyāmi vākpate tava saṃnidhau yadā vācogataṃ sarvaṃ tava vāci samāhitam
english: And what shall I declare in your presence, O Lord of Speech, when all that can be uttered is already gathered within your own speech?

sanskrit: yad dhi kiṃ cit kṛtaṃ loke kartavyaṃ kriyate ca yat tvattas tan niḥsṛtaṃ deva lokā buddhimayā hi te
english: For whatever has been done in the world, whatever is to be done and is being done, all of it has issued forth from you, O god; the worlds are made of your understanding.

sanskrit: kathayed devalokaṃ yo devarājasamīpataḥ dharmakāmārthaśāstrāṇāṃ so 'rthān brūyāt tavāgrataḥ
english: He who would describe the world of the gods in the very presence of the king of the gods—such a one would be expounding the matters of the sciences of dharma, pleasure, and wealth before you.

sanskrit: śarābhighātād vyathitaṃ mano me madhusūdana gātrāṇi cāvasīdanti na ca buddhiḥ prasīdati
english: My mind is troubled by the striking of the arrows, O slayer of Madhu; my limbs sink, and my understanding does not grow clear.

sanskrit: na ca me pratibhā kā cid asti kiṃ cit prabhāṣitum pīḍyamānasya govinda viṣānalasamaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Nor have I any flash of insight to speak even a little, O Govinda, tormented as I am by arrows like poison and fire.

sanskrit: balaṃ medhāḥ prajarati prāṇāḥ saṃtvarayanti ca marmāṇi paritapyante bhrāntaṃ cetas tathaiva ca
english: My strength wanes, my wit decays, and my life-breaths hasten away; my vital points burn, and my mind is likewise bewildered.

sanskrit: daurbalyāt sajjate vāṅ me sa kathaṃ vaktum utsahe sādhu me tvaṃ prasīdasva dāśārhakulanandana
english: From weakness my speech falters; how then shall I dare to speak? Be gracious to me, I pray, O delight of the house of the Dāśārhas.

sanskrit: tat kṣamasva mahābāho na brūyāṃ kiṃ cid acyuta tvatsaṃnidhau ca sīdeta vācaspatir api bruvan
english: Forgive me therefore, O mighty-armed Acyuta, that I should say nothing at all; even Vācaspati, speaking in your presence, would falter.

sanskrit: na diśaḥ saṃprajānāmi nākāśaṃ na ca medinīm kevalaṃ tava vīryeṇa tiṣṭhāmi madhusūdana
english: I no longer rightly know the quarters, nor the sky, nor the earth; it is solely by your power that I endure, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: svayam eva prabho tasmād dharmarājasya yad dhitam tad bravīhy āśu sarveṣām āgamānāṃ tvam āgamaḥ
english: Therefore, O lord, do you yourself speak swiftly that which is for the good of the King of Dharma; for you are the source of all sources of sacred lore.

sanskrit: kathaṃ tvayi sthite loke śāśvate lokakartari prabrūyān madvidhaḥ kaś cid gurau śiṣya iva sthite
english: How, when you abide—you the eternal, the maker of the worlds—could anyone such as I hold forth, as a pupil might in the presence of his teacher?

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca upapannam idaṃ vākyaṃ kauravāṇāṃ dhuraṃdhare mahāvīrye mahāsattve sthite sarvārthadarśini
english: Vāsudeva said: Fitting is this speech in you, O bearer of the Kauravas' burden, of mighty valor, of great inner strength, who perceive all things.

sanskrit: yac ca mām āttha gāṅgeya bāṇaghātarujaṃ prati gṛhāṇātra varaṃ bhīṣma matprasādakṛtaṃ vibho
english: And as for what you have told me, O son of Gaṅgā, concerning the pain of the arrows' striking—accept herein a boon, O Bhīṣma, granted by my grace, O lord.

sanskrit: na te glānir na te mūrchā na dāho na ca te rujā prabhaviṣyanti gāṅgeya kṣutpipāse na cāpy uta
english: No faintness, no swoon, no burning, no pain shall overcome you, O son of Gaṅgā, nor yet hunger and thirst.

sanskrit: jñānāni ca samagrāṇi pratibhāsyanti te 'nagha na ca te kva cid āsaktir buddheḥ prādurbhaviṣyati
english: All forms of knowledge shall shine forth within you, O sinless one, nor shall any clinging of the intellect arise in you anywhere.

sanskrit: sattvasthaṃ ca mano nityaṃ tava bhīṣma bhaviṣyati rajas tamobhyāṃ rahitaṃ ghanair mukta ivoḍurāṭ
english: And your mind, O Bhīṣma, shall ever abide in the quality of sattva, freed from passion and darkness, like the lord of stars released from the clouds.

sanskrit: yad yac ca dharmasaṃyuktam arthayuktam athāpi vā cintayiṣyasi tatrāgryā buddhis tava bhaviṣyati
english: And whatever you ponder that is joined to dharma, or to wealth as well, in that your understanding shall be foremost.

sanskrit: imaṃ ca rājaśārdūla bhūtagrāmaṃ caturvidham cakṣur divyaṃ samāśritya drakṣyasy amitavikrama
english: And this fourfold host of beings, O tiger among kings, you shall behold, O man of boundless prowess, by recourse to the divine eye.

sanskrit: caturvidhaṃ prajājālaṃ saṃyukto jñānacakṣuṣā bhīṣma drakṣyasi tattvena jale mīna ivāmale
english: Endowed with the eye of knowledge, O Bhīṣma, you shall behold the fourfold web of creatures in their very truth, as a fish is seen in clear water.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te vyāsasahitāḥ sarva eva maharṣayaḥ ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃyuktair vacobhiḥ kṛṣṇam arcayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then all those great seers, together with Vyāsa, worshipped Kṛṣṇa with words joined to the Ṛc, Yajus, and Sāman.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvārtavaṃ divyaṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ nabhastalāt papāta yatra vārṣṇeyaḥ sagāṅgeyaḥ sapāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then a divine rain of flowers of every season fell from the vault of heaven upon the place where the Vārṣṇeya was, together with the son of Gaṅgā and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: vāditrāṇi ca divyāni jaguś cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ na cāhitam aniṣṭaṃ vā kiṃ cit tatra vyadṛśyata
english: And celestial instruments sounded, and the troops of apsarases sang; nor was anything harmful or unwelcome seen there at all.

sanskrit: vavau śivaḥ sukho vāyuḥ sarvagandhavahaḥ śuciḥ śāntāyāṃ diśi śāntāś ca prāvadan mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
english: An auspicious, gentle, pure breeze blew, bearing every fragrance; and toward the quarter grown calm the beasts and birds cried out, themselves at peace.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād bhagavān sahasrāṃśur divākaraḥ dahan vanam ivaikānte pratīcyāṃ pratyadṛśyata
english: Then, after a moment, the blessed thousand-rayed day-maker appeared in the west, as though burning a forest at the world's far edge.

sanskrit: tato maharṣayaḥ sarve samutthāya janārdanam bhīṣmam āmantrayāṃ cakrū rājānaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Then all the great seers rose up and took leave of Janārdana, of Bhīṣma, and of King Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tataḥ praṇāmam akarot keśavaḥ pāṇḍavas tathā sātyakiḥ saṃjayaś caiva sa ca śāradvataḥ kṛpaḥ
english: Then Keśava made obeisance, and so did the Pāṇḍava, and Sātyaki and Saṃjaya, and Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat.

sanskrit: tatas te dharmaniratāḥ samyak tair abhipūjitāḥ śvaḥ sameṣyāma ity uktvā yatheṣṭaṃ tvaritā yayuḥ
english: Then those devoted to dharma, duly honored by the seers, said "Tomorrow we shall meet again," and went their ways in haste, each as he pleased.

sanskrit: tathaivāmantrya gāṅgeyaṃ keśavas te ca pāṇḍavāḥ pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtya rathān āruruhuḥ śubhān
english: In the same way, having taken leave of the son of Gaṅgā, Keśava and the Pāṇḍavas, turning round him to the right, mounted their splendid chariots.

sanskrit: tato rathaiḥ kāñcanadantakūbarair; mahīdharābhaiḥ samadaiś ca dantibhiḥ hayaiḥ suparṇair iva cāśugāmibhiḥ; padātibhiś cāttaśarāsanādibhiḥ
english: Then with chariots whose poles were of gold and ivory, with rutting elephants like mountains, with swift-going horses like Suparṇa, and with foot soldiers bearing bows and the rest—

sanskrit: yayau rathānāṃ purato hi sā camūs; tathaiva paścād atimātrasāriṇī puraś ca paścāc ca yathā mahānadī; purarkṣavantaṃ girim etya narmadā
english: that army moved on, vast in its march, both before the chariots and behind them likewise, as the great river Narmadā flows before and behind on reaching the mountain that abounds in bears.

sanskrit: tataḥ purastād bhagavān niśākaraḥ; samutthitas tām abhiharṣayaṃś camūm divākarāpītarasās tathauṣadhīḥ; punaḥ svakenaiva guṇena yojayan
english: Then the blessed maker of night rose up before them, gladdening that host, and joining once more with their own virtue the herbs whose sap the day-maker had drunk up.

sanskrit: tataḥ puraṃ surapurasaṃnibhadyuti; praviśya te yaduvṛṣapāṇḍavās tadā yathocitān bhavanavarān samāviśañ; śramānvitā mṛgapatayo guhā iva
english: Then those bulls of the Yadus and the Pāṇḍavas, entering the city whose radiance rivaled the city of the gods, withdrew each to his own fitting and stately mansion, weary, as lions withdraw to their dens.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ praviśya bhavanaṃ prasupto madhusūdanaḥ yāmamātrāvaśeṣāyāṃ yāminyāṃ pratyabudhyata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having entered his dwelling, the slayer of Madhu fell asleep, and awoke when but a single watch of the night remained.

sanskrit: sa dhyānapatham āśritya sarvajñānāni mādhavaḥ avalokya tataḥ paścād dadhyau brahma sanātanam
english: Mādhava, taking to the path of meditation, surveyed all forms of knowledge, and thereafter meditated upon the eternal brahman.

sanskrit: tataḥ śrutipurāṇajñāḥ śikṣitā raktakaṇṭhinaḥ astuvan viśvakarmāṇaṃ vāsudevaṃ prajāpatim
english: Then those versed in scripture and ancient lore, well trained and sweet of throat, sang the praises of Vāsudeva, the maker of all, the Lord of creatures.

sanskrit: paṭhanti pāṇisvanikās tathā gāyanti gāyanāḥ śaṅkhānakamṛdaṅgāṃś ca pravādyanta sahasraśaḥ
english: Those who keep time by clapping recited, and the singers sang, and conches, drums, and tabors were sounded by the thousand.

sanskrit: vīṇāpaṇavaveṇūnāṃ svanaś cātimanoramaḥ prahāsa iva vistīrṇaḥ śuśruve tasya veśmanaḥ
english: And the most enchanting sound of lutes, small drums, and flutes, spread wide like a peal of laughter, was heard from his mansion.

sanskrit: tathā yudhiṣṭhirasyāpi rājño maṅgalasaṃhitāḥ uccerur madhurā vāco gītavāditrasaṃhitāḥ
english: And likewise from King Yudhiṣṭhira's dwelling there rose up sweet voices charged with benediction, blended with song and instrument.

sanskrit: tata utthāya dāśārhaḥ snātaḥ prāñjalir acyutaḥ japtvā guhyaṃ mahābāhur agnīn āśritya tasthivān
english: Then the Dāśārha, the mighty-armed Acyuta, having risen and bathed, with palms joined, having murmured the secret prayer, stood by attending upon the sacred fires.
